declared: 2026-11-08, before the frozen rustc 1.98.0 oracle of these exact bytes and before any candidate run of these bytes. The shapes reduce census 12's crate record "minimal specialization introduces a non-marker predicate" at core's `SpecNextChunk` pair (array/mod.rs:1044 and 1062, located by the analysis-only diagnostic obj/parallel/census-batch11/diagnostics/d9-marker). Exploration drafts with other bytes (obj/parallel/census-batch11/repro/maybe-const/) were run first: rustc 1.98.0 accepted the core pair, the pair with a plain marker supertrait, a `[const]` child over an ordinary parent bound and the ordinary pair; the census 12 pin rejected the first three with the census message. Each outcome follows the rule read in the pinned rustc 1.98.0 sources (compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/hir_ty_lowering/mod.rs, which lowers a `[const] Tr` bound to the ordinary `Tr` clause of predicates_of and its constness only to const_conditions, and a `const Tr` bound to `Tr` plus a HostEffect clause; compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/impl_wf_check/min_specialization.rs `check_predicates`, which compares elaborated predicates_of only, and `check_specialization_on`, which allows a Trait clause on a `rustc_unsafe_specialization_marker` trait and rejects any other clause, a HostEffect clause included, unless it is global; compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/traits/specialize/mod.rs `specializes`, which requires a conditionally const child for a conditionally const parent and proves the parent's const_conditions as `[const]` HostEffect goals under the child's param-env; compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/traits/coherence.rs, where impls that overlap without that ordering conflict, E0119)

core-next-chunk.rs.reason: core's shape: `const impl<I: [const] Iterator<Item = T>, T, const N: usize> SpecNextChunk<T, N> for I` and a child adding `TrustedLen`, `const unsafe trait TrustedLen: [const] Iterator` with `#[rustc_unsafe_specialization_marker]`; both impls' predicates_of hold the ordinary `I: Iterator`, so the child adds only the marker

plain-marker-supertrait.rs.reason: the same pair with `unsafe trait TrustedLen: Iterator`

child-only-const.rs.reason: an ordinary parent bound `I: Iterator<Item = T>` and a child `I: [const] Iterator<Item = T> + TrustedLen`; the child's `[const]` is a const condition, not a predicate, and the parent is const in every case the child is

ordinary-pair.rs.reason: control: the same pair as ordinary impls with ordinary bounds

child-not-const.rs.reason: opponent: core's parent beside an ordinary child impl `impl<I: Iterator<Item = T> + TrustedLen, ..>`; the parent is conditionally const and the child is not, so the child does not specialize and the impls conflict (E0119)

child-weaker-const.rs.reason: opponent: core's parent beside a const child with only ordinary bounds, `const impl<I: Iterator<Item = T> + TrustedLen, ..>`; the parent's const condition `I: [const] Iterator` does not hold under the child's param-env, so the child does not specialize (E0119)

const-marker-bound.rs.reason: opponent: a child `const impl<I: [const] Iterator<Item = T> + const Exact, ..>` over a `const unsafe trait Exact` marker; `const Exact` adds a HostEffect clause the parent lacks, which is never a marker clause
